section: 1. Introduction
units: Welcome to the Faculty of Computing and Digital Technology of HELP University (HELP).

This Postgraduate Student Handbook (the Handbook) outlines the academic and administrative structure for all postgraduate candidates of the faculty, stipulating HELP policy and procedure, subject to regulatory guidelines, for your programme progression and completion.

Undertaking a postgraduate programme successfully as an adult with a career, family and personal commitments is a challenging task. It requires physical and intellectual stamina, commitment, discipline and good time management; resulting in competence, confidence and networking advantage, among other attributes that you will gain, for an enriching and rewarding career and for success in life.

section: 2. Welcome Note from the Dean
units: The Faculty of Computing and Digital Technology (formerly the Faculty of Applied Sciences and Multimedia) was established in 1998 to prepare individuals for a rewarding career in computing. Information and digital technologies are now part of daily life in a way that could not be envisioned in 1998. In particular, digital technologies and business performance are inextricably interwoven. Digital technologies continue to develop with breathtaking and disruptive rapidity, with a continuing significant and urgent demand for qualified, competent and creative professionals.

High organisational performance can be built on alliances and partnerships. HELP has forged robust links with institutions of higher learning in more than 30 countries, with many partners across Asia and Europe. The strength of HELP's own and collaborative programmes has also enabled HELP scholars to obtain PhD scholarships from the world's top universities in the UK and Australia.

section: 4. Mission, Vision and Values > 4.5 Teaching Philosophy and Pedagogy
units: Teaching Philosophy
At HELP University, we focus on four capabilities that underpin all levels of study:
The Skill of Conceptualisation
The Science of Organisation
The Art of Articulation
The Practice of Application
Pedagogy

HELP's success lies in its unique educational philosophy and pedagogy. Firmly believing that education is an opportunity for an individual to realise his or her fullest potential in order to reach the pinnacle of his or her vocation and to lead a meaningful and fulfilling life, we utilise our faculty's impeccable academic credentials and vast experience in all levels and modes of education to design and deliver programmes that live up to the highest standards.

At postgraduate level this is expressed through supervised independent enquiry, seminar-based discussion, applied project work and research-informed teaching. Candidates are expected to take substantial responsibility for their own learning, and academic staff act as facilitators, supervisors and critical readers of that work.

section: 4. Mission, Vision and Values > 4.6 Quality Assurance
units: HELP's reputation as a university of achievers has earned it a worldwide standing. The high standards that it has painstakingly achieved are guaranteed, and where necessary enhanced, through a system of quality assurance by HELP's partner universities and statutory requirements. HELP was the first private institution of higher learning to obtain ISO 9001:2000 under AJA. Currently, the certification body for HELP's ISO 9001:2015 is NQA. In addition, since June 2020, HELP has been certified to ISO 45001:2018.

Quality assurance in HELP is based on a system of internal and external peer scrutiny. The principles of quality assurance in HELP are based on a developmental approach and are viewed as a shared responsibility executed in a centralised and decentralised manner. Whilst the Vice-Chancellor and senior management staff play a major role in steering the University's quality assurance system, all members of the University community are entrusted to recognise and promulgate best quality practices.

section: 5. Postgraduate Programmes > 5.1 General Provisions for Postgraduate Candidature
units: Course Progression

Candidates are advised that unless personal or professional commitments necessitate the deferment of one or more subjects, it is in their interest to complete the programme as scheduled. If one or more subject deferments need to be made, candidates are still expected to complete the programme within the maximum duration stated for their programme.

Candidates who exceed the maximum duration and wish to continue must obtain approval for continuation. Such an extension shall not exceed the maximum duration from commencement of the programme. A continuation fee of RM2,000.00 is chargeable for each year beyond the standard duration, up to a maximum of an additional two years. The rate is subject to change without notice.

section: 5. Postgraduate Programmes > 5.1 General Provisions for Postgraduate Candidature
units: Assessment of student learning is a key aspect of quality assurance and one of the most important measures used to demonstrate the achievement of learning outcomes. It is therefore crucial that appropriate assessment methods and mechanisms are in place. Qualifications are awarded based on the results of assessment. The methods of student assessment must be clear, consistent, effective, reliable and in line with current practices, and must clearly measure the achievement of the intended learning outcomes (COPPA, 2nd Edition, 2017).

All candidates are required to pass BOTH the continuous and the final assessment components of every module, based on the passing marks defined for that module. A pass implies that the examiner is satisfied that the candidate has met all the learning outcomes of that particular module.

section: 5. Postgraduate Programmes > 5.2 Master of Data Science (R/0613/7/0045) (07/30) (MQA/FA13820)
units: The programme aims to produce graduates who meet the growing demand for data science professionals capable of making decisions based on the availability of comprehensive data. It prepares graduates to apply analytics techniques for knowledge discovery and dissemination, to assist researchers or decision-makers in achieving organisational objectives.
Objectives
The objectives of the Master of Data Science are to produce graduates who are able to:
Apply quantitative modelling and data analysis techniques to the solution of real-world business problems, communicate findings, and effectively present results using data visualisation techniques.
Recognise and analyse ethical issues in business related to intellectual property, data security, integrity and privacy.
Demonstrate knowledge of statistical data analysis techniques utilised in decision-making.
Use data mining software to solve real-world problems.
Employ cutting-edge tools and technologies to analyse Big Data.
Apply algorithms to build machine intelligence.
Demonstrate teamwork, leadership skills and decision-making.

units: The programme aims to produce graduates who meet the growing demand for cybersecurity professionals capable of securing the confidentiality, integrity and availability of comprehensive data and information. It prepares graduates to apply analytics techniques for knowledge discovery and dissemination, to assist researchers or decision-makers in achieving organisational objectives.
Objectives
The Master of Cybersecurity is an Open and Distance Learning (ODL) programme designed with the following objectives:
Comprehensive Knowledge: Equip candidates with a thorough understanding of cybersecurity principles, practices and technologies.
Skill Development: Foster technical skills in areas such as threat analysis, incident response and risk management.
Critical Thinking: Encourage analytical and critical thinking to assess security challenges and devise effective solutions.
Ethical Framework: Instil a strong ethical foundation for addressing cybersecurity issues, including legal and regulatory compliance.
Real-World Application: Provide practical experience through case studies, simulations and projects that reflect current cybersecurity trends and threats.
Collaboration and Communication: Enhance teamwork and communication skills essential for working in diverse cybersecurity environments.

section: 6. Grading Scheme > 6.2 Doctoral Programmes
units: This section applies to both research doctorates offered by the faculty — the Doctor of Philosophy in Computing and the Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science. Each is a research-based degree, which consists of a mandatory Research Methodology module and the Thesis. Candidates must pass both components:
The Research Methodology module consists of several assessments, and candidates need to achieve an overall pass mark for the module.

Research progress during the Thesis component is monitored through several periodic progress assessments. Candidates must pass all periodic assessments and may be withdrawn from the programme if progress is unsatisfactory.
The final assessment for the award of the degree is through the thesis examination and viva voce, conducted by a panel of internal and external examiners.
There is no GPA or CGPA calculation for the PhD programmes. Award of the degree is dependent on passing all the components listed above.

units: Transfer of credits may be granted based on subjects completed in equivalent courses conducted at educational institutions recognised by HELP University. section: 9. Policies and Regulations > 9.1 Registration
units: Every candidate is required to complete an official registration every semester. Candidates who fail to complete the registration process are not considered officially enrolled and will be denied the opportunity of complete modules at the end of the semester. Candidates shall confirm their subject enrolment by Week 0 of each semester and shall be enrolled for the subject if payment has already been made. If the fee is not paid, no enrolment shall be made.

Once registration is completed, candidates retain one copy of the form and the Assistant Registrar will issue an invoice, which is used when making payment.

section: 10. Programme Administration > 10.2 Prerequisites
units: Subject prerequisites are listed in this Handbook in the Subject Descriptions. These requirements are intended to ensure that candidates have a reasonable chance of completing a module without a low grade or a fail grade. A prerequisite is a module that must be taken and passed prior to registering for any of the modules that require it.

Any candidate who has failed the first of a sequence of modules is not allowed to enrol in the subsequent module until the fail grade has been changed to a pass grade. Candidates may refer to the respective programme proforma for subject prerequisites.
Candidates holding a non-Computing degree are advised to seek advice and/or counselling from the faculty regarding prerequisite module(s) before enrolling in their postgraduate programme.

section: 10. Programme Administration > 10.6 Withdrawal Procedure from HELP University
units: A candidate shall be deemed to be no longer enrolled in a programme at HELP University if the candidate has completed the requirements for that programme; if registration in the programme has been terminated; or if the candidate has been excluded on academic or disciplinary grounds.

Any candidate who wishes to discontinue or withdraw from HELP University should inform the University immediately in writing. A withdrawal form, available at the Registry or the Faculty, must be completed and submitted to the faculty for processing.

A candidate who has registered but does not attend class for one month from the date of commencement or enrolment shall be classified as having withdrawn unofficially, and all fees except the resource fee and the security deposit shall be forfeited.

All work submitted for assessment must be the candidate's own, and all sources consulted must be properly acknowledged using the referencing convention specified in the module outline. Plagiarism, collusion, fabrication of data, and the undisclosed use of generative artificial intelligence tools in contravention of the stated module policy are treated as academic misconduct and are dealt with under the University's disciplinary procedures.

section: 12. Academic Consultations
units: Academic consultation is an integral part of a candidate's academic experience. Academic advisors can provide support and guidance to candidates who seek their service, but it is also the responsibility of each candidate to be familiar with academic policies and regulations and to take responsibility for their studies at HELP University.

An academic advisor offers candidates information, guidance and advice throughout their postgraduate programme. Specifically, academic advisors assist candidates in identifying programme requirements and help them balance their module load each semester, so that they do not take too many demanding modules in one semester. Candidates are also informed of modules that require prerequisites or carry other restrictions before registration.

New candidates are informed about the education system and its requirements through a series of briefings conducted every semester. Candidates are encouraged to make an appointment to seek advice from an academic advisor to discuss important educational issues and matters pertaining to their progression.

section: 13. Research Candidature and Supervision > 13.1 Appointment of Supervisors
units: Every research candidate is assigned a principal supervisor, and where appropriate a co-supervisor, appointed by the faculty on the basis of disciplinary fit with the candidate's proposed area of research. The principal supervisor holds primary responsibility for guiding the candidate's research design, monitoring progress and advising on the preparation of the thesis or report. Where a project is conducted with an industry partner, an additional industry supervisor may be appointed.

A change of supervisor may be requested by either the candidate or the supervisor and is subject to the approval of the Head of School and the Faculty Postgraduate Committee. Such a request should be made in writing, stating the reasons, and will normally be considered only where the change is in the academic interest of the candidate.

section: 14. Subject Descriptions > 14.1 Master of Data Science
units: MDS501 Programming for Data Science

This module equips candidates with the fundamentals of programming using a high-level programming language to solve problems focusing on data. The module covers various data analysis and processing techniques such as retrieval, extraction, conversion, aggregation, filtering, processing and storing, using programming libraries and toolkits.
MDS502 Data Management

This module introduces techniques related to the modelling, extraction, cleansing, profiling, integration and access of data. It then introduces the role of databases and database management systems, covering relational and non-relational databases. Policies for access and sharing, including provisions for the appropriate protection of privacy, ethics, confidentiality, security and other requirements, are also discussed.
MDS503 Statistics for Data Science

This module introduces basic statistical concepts and methods, including simple and multiple linear regression, classification, decision trees, support vector machines, and unsupervised learning. In addition, the module serves as an introduction to implementing these methods through the use of statistical software.
MDS504 Applied Machine Learning
